summary: Intermittent tenant routing to standby variant during canary ramp caused by TLS session-ticket rotation + connection-pool reuse
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged canary ramp for customer Finly Health (dedicated pool in prod/us-east) a small but measurable percentage (~0.8-1.2%) of requests were routed to the standby/degraded variant despite an explicit tenant-level model pin. Affected requests were concentrated on long-lived streaming sessions and multipart/chunked inputs. Impact: mixed model outputs and billing discrepancy for the customer; customer reported sporadic lower-quality responses and two failed production jobs.

Impact:
- Finly Health: intermittent degraded responses, 2 production jobs failed to meet QA checks during window (2026-03-10 02:30-03:40 UTC).
- Estimated request surface impacted: ~0.8-1.2% of their requests during canary weight step.
- Business risk: medium (customer SLA: dedicated, some jobs are high-sensitivity).

Observed behavior:
- Tenant remained pinned at control plane (pin record visible in config DB and snapshot).
- Orchestrator snapshot and serving runtime showed correct model assignment for >99% of connections.
- Edge-proxy connection logs show some long-lived keep-alive connections reused after TLS session-ticket rotation; when reused the request headers contained a stale edge-cohort cookie which mapped to standby cohort.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant pin must be honored end-to-end; connection reuse should not allow cross-cohort routing for pinned tenants.

Steps to reproduce (attempted by SRE):
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a tenant pin to guanaco-13b-q4_0 in control plane and verify snapshot commit
2) Start sustained streaming sessions from a client that multiplexes several requests over a single keep-alive connection
3) Trigger TLS session-ticket rotation on the edge (simulated) and observe which cohort mapping the subsequent requests resolve to
4) Observe routing logs at edge-proxy and check for reused connections with stale edge-cohort cookie or header
5) Compare to orchestrator and serving-runtime snapshots to verify pin presence
logs_and_metrics: Edge proxy connection logs (edge-proxy-logs-2026-03-10-02.gz) show 'conn-id=abc123 reuse after ticket-rotate, cookie=cohort-standby' lines at 02:44:23 UTC. Control plane snapshot audit (snapshot-2026-03-10-02:30.json) shows tenant pin committed to primary variant. Trace sample: request-id=finly-req-7f4a -> routed to standby variant at edge. Tokenized cost spike + partial quality delta visible in Canary QA dashboard (dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CanaryQA/finly-health).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: pin replication lag between control plane snapshot commit and edge cache was considered but ruled out (timestamps show snapshot available before observed misroutes). Deeper trace shows a correlation with TLS session-ticket rotation events on the edge (ticket rotate cron at 02:44:22 UTC) and connection-pool behavior where connections were returned to the pool and later reused for requests from the same tenant, but the cookie/header used for cohort mapping had been rewritten by an old proxy process earlier in the connection's lifetime. Edge's connection reuse logic currently does not enforce per-connection cohort revalidation after session-ticket rotation.

Partial findings:
- Orchestrator and serving runtime correctly honored pin for new connections.
- Reused keep-alive connections after ticket rotation occasionally presented stale edge-cohort mapping metadata.
- This behavior disproportionately affected streaming/long-poll clients and chunked/multipart requests.

Hypothesis: TLS ticket rotation can cause connection reinitialization paths that interact with the proxy's connection reuse cache in a way that preserves stale cohort metadata on a connection. When that connection is later used for a pinned tenant, the edge cohort resolver can return the standby cohort mapping instead of re-resolving against the fresh snapshot.

Evidence collected:
- Packet captures and edge-proxy logs attached in internal artifact storage (s3://redwood-artifacts/SUP-2098765/).
- Canary QA dashboard and billing spike graph attached.

Next steps being executed:
- Temporary mitigation: disabled TLS ticket rotation during the active canary window for prod/us-east (applied 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC) and invalidated conn-pool entries for the customer (conn-pool shard flush).
- Longer-term fix: changes to edge-proxy connection pool to force revalidation of cohort mapping after ticket rotation OR tag connections with cohort snapshot version and reject reuse across snapshot-version boundaries. Proposed PR: github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/1291 (edge connection-pool patch).
- Deployment plan: staged rollout in us-east + eu-west with monitoring for regression (controlled canary).
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer alert received 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC complaining about 'sporadic degraded outputs' during a scheduled canary. Opened ticket and escalated to SRE.
Finly Health (customer): Provided request-ids finly-req-7f4a and finly-req-7f4b and sample transcripts showing lower-quality output. They've paused non-critical jobs until behavior stabilizes.
SRE (Tomás Vega): Confirmed correlation with TLS ticket rotation and edge conn-pool reuse. Implemented conn-pool flush for Finly's tenant and disabled rotation during canary window as mitigation.
Engineer (Evelyn Park): Drafted PR to add cohort-version tags to connections; running unit + integration tests. Scheduling canary for PR roll-forward after peer review.

Support (Aisha): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and asked for confirmation on whether degraded outputs stopped after 03:10 UTC. Customer acknowledged partial improvement but reported two lingering failed jobs (logs attached).
workaround: 1) Flushed edge conn-pool entries for the affected tenant group (done 2026-03-10 03:06 UTC). 2) Temporarily disabled TLS session-ticket rotation in prod/us-east for the canary window (03:05-03:40 UTC). 3) If customer sees issues, advise reconnecting streaming sessions to force new connections. These mitigations reduced misroutes to <0.05% in the observation window.
resolution: In progress: temporary mitigations applied and customer provided partial confirmation. Permanent fix will be to land PR github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/1291 to tag/revalidate cohort on reuse and a small orchestrator guard to prevent serving of standby variant for explicitly pinned tenants irrespective of edge cohort when connection metadata is ambiguous. Targeted deployment: us-east (canary) 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-18 after monitoring. Postmortem scheduled (Confluence page above) and billing adjustment in progress for Finly Health for impacted requests.
next_steps: 1) Complete PR review and integration tests for edge-proxy PR (#1291). 2) Add orchestrator safeguard (PR #871) to prefer explicit pin over edge cohort in ambiguous cases. 3) Run a controlled canary in us-east and eu-west; monitor Canary QA and routing correctness metrics. 4) Create postmortem and notify billing/CS for customer crediting. 5) Follow up with Finly Health on 2026-03-13.
public_notes: Customer notified of temporary mitigation and planned permanent fix. Will follow up with postmortem and billing adjusment if root cause confirmed.
